title: When Is a Relation Worth Trusting? Manipulation Costs, Exposure, and the Trust Trap in Multi-Relational Graph Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.37239v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Multi-relational graph detectors learn from clean data how much to trust each relation, but an adversary pays a different price to manipulate each relation and each action; taking such costs as given, we ask when using a relation is worse than ignoring it. Our first main result proves that degree gating strictly beats every selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and that this window is sharp; on real graphs, validated gating gains exactly on the relations that meet these conditions and nowhere else. Our second shows that a per-node exposure bound, which extends to message passing, tells a platform which relation to harden: exposure per unit cost, computed without any attack, picks the relation whose hardening raises the exact trap threshold most in 15 of 16 cases, against at most 7 for informativeness, cheapness, or an analysis with equal edi

translated_title: 何时值得信任一种关系？多关系图学习中的操纵成本、暴露度与信任陷阱
translated_abstract: 多关系图检测器从干净数据中学习对每种关系应给予多大的信任，但对手操纵每种关系、每个动作所需付出的代价各不相同；在将这些成本视为既定的前提下，我们探讨了何时使用某种关系反而比忽略它更糟糕。我们的第一个主要结果证明：当一部分样本被隔离在某种关系上、且攻击者无力打开这道“门”时，度门控严格优于对该关系的任何选择或重加权方案，并且这一窗口是紧致的；在真实图上，经验证的门控恰好只在满足这些条件的关系上取得收益，而在其他地方没有收益。我们的第二个结果表明，一种可扩展到消息传递的逐节点暴露度上界能够告诉平台应当加固哪种关系：无需任何攻击即可计算出的“单位成本暴露度”，在16个案例中的15个里选中的正是加固后能最大程度提高精确陷阱阈值的关系，而基于信息量、低成本或等努力分析的准则至多只能选中7个。
tldr: 该论文以对手操纵成本为前提，证明了当部分人群被隔离于某关系且攻击者无力打开该门控时，度门控严格优于任何关系选择或重加权方案，并提出无需攻击即可计算的逐节点“单位成本暴露度”指标，能准确指导平台选择应加固哪种关系以最大化提升信任陷阱阈值。
en_tdlr: This paper proves that degree gating strictly beats any selection or reweighting of a relation when part of the population is isolated on it and the attacker cannot afford to open the gate, and introduces an attack-free, per-node exposure-per-unit-cost bound that accurately identifies which relation a platform should harden to most raise the trust trap threshold.
